runs.question: What change to the NIST AI RMF does America's AI Action Plan recommend, and which characteristics of trustworthy AI does the AI RMF itself list?

answer.text:
I couldn't find anything in the provided passages about what America's AI Action Plan recommends for the NIST AI RMF, so that part of your question is unanswered here. The passages also don't include the Action Plan itself.

On the trustworthiness characteristics, the NIST AI 100-1 passages give a partial list. The Framework's Part 1 is where the characteristics of trustworthy AI systems are outlined As the AI RMF is put into use, additional lessons will be learned to inform future updates and additional resources. The list itself appears in the passage that follows. It names the aim of being valid and reliable, safe, and secure and resilient. It also names being accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy enhanced, and fair with harmful biases managed valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy enhanced, and fair with their harmful biases managed. The passage's opening words are cut off, so I can't confirm the full wording of the list or whether it is complete.

On change, the AI RMF's own update process is described separately. NIST treats the Framework as a living document. NIST will review the content and usefulness of the Framework regularly to determine if an update is appropriate. A formal review is expected no later than 2028. This describes NIST's own schedule, not a recommendation from the Action Plan.
